text:
Where does the harsh road lead me

        through steps of costly warning?

        To leave scattered on the wind

        just complaints against time and fate.


        If I look back at my error and madness,

        chastening is no small reward,

        but how feeling tyrannizes

        when it drives understanding itself from reason!


        Let the will leave captivity,

        for free will must not idolize

        the most sensitive part of harms.


        The fates will decipher the mystery,

        and my warning will remain, freed

        from another's delirium, in disillusions.

translation.title: Disillusion
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's moral vocabulary of chastening, will, fate, and disillusion.
